title: Fixed Crossed Leg and Open V Log Cradle
description: One newly authored complete fixed empty sawbuck-style log cradle. Two separated end stations each have two whole long crossing timber legs; the same four members continue well above their transverse pins to form two genuinely open V-shaped upper cradles. Two continuous low longitudinal ties join the end stations below the crossing levels, while independent short lower stop straps hold the fixed spread. Four complete grounded pads and whole side pivot caps finish the unified stand. There is deliberately no top beam, tabletop, work plank, split vise jaw or lead-screw mechanism. Unlike the old four splayed legs converging below a flat sawhorse beam, the upper load-outline is an open V at both ends and the long space between them stays empty; unlike the folding split-jaw bench its crossed legs continue into the cradle rather than ending under a flat clamp bed. Entire numeric geometry newly authored, no old legs extracted or extended. Three opaque constant PBR roles, metres Z up and whole ground-centred origin, one whole prop zero scenes. Empty static art only: no timber, saw, chain, folding movement, spread adjustment, log fit, sawing, work holding, load, strength, manufacture, stability or equipment safety capability. Rigging animation interaction not made.
